Y.comment: Faithful overall. The small embellishments ('widowed', 'stepmother', 'fresh fish') add details the source does not give.

additions: 'stepmother' for Wang Xiang's 母
sense_errors: 'shielding the coffin with his body' for 以身捍火 (he shielded against the fire)
'without his cap properly adjusted' for 不冠 (not wearing a cap)
names_garbled: 鍾 rendered as 'large jars' instead of the zhong capacity measure
Z.comment: Complete. It has a few minor inaccuracies: the zhong measure, the cap and the shielding clause.

W.comment: Complete and accurate. All entries are rendered faithfully, including Xu Zi's story up to the break at the page edge.

names_garbled: 'Fang Chu, courtesy name Mingyou': the courtesy name is Ming; 幼 means 'in childhood'
'Biographies of Filial Sons from Wide and Beneficent Gatherings': 蕭廣濟 is the author Xiao Guangji, wrongly read as part of the title
X.comment: Content is accurate, but it garbles a courtesy name and turns the author Xiao Guangji's name into part of the book title.

sense_errors: 'having exhausted his resources on the mourning rites' is a doubtful reading of 承父資喪
Y.comment: Faithful and complete. The only weak spot is a loose interpretation of the Zong Cheng clause.

additions: 'his mother's tomb': 'mother' is not in the source
names_garbled: 'Records of the Grand Administrator of Huayang' mistranslates 華陽國志 (Records of the States South of Mount Hua)
Z.comment: Accurate overall. It mistranslates the title Huayang guozhi and adds that the tomb was his mother's in the Cai Yong entry.

W.comment: Complete and accurate. The 'By' in the header is a small slip.

X.comment: Complete and accurate. 'Any external blame' is a loose rendering of 復將何尤 but acceptable.

Y.comment: Complete and accurate. 'Deep water' adds a small gloss but is harmless.

Z.comment: Complete. 'Taking the solid as master' correctly finishes the broken phrase from the previous page. 'Able husband' for 士夫 is loose but acceptable.

sense_errors: 'The commentaries apply this to' treats 訓注 (Li Xun and Zheng Zhu) as 'commentaries', so two of the four examples are lost
names_garbled: Baiyun is glossed as Kong Wuzhong; 白雲 is Guo Yong
W.comment: Faithful otherwise, but it misreads 訓注 as 'commentaries' and misidentifies Baiyun.

names_garbled: Baiyun is glossed as the Chan master Baiyun Shouduan; it is Guo Yong
Xun Zhu is glossed as 'Zheng Xun and Li Zhu'; they are Li Xun and Zheng Zhu
X.comment: The only version that correctly reads 訓注 as people, but its glosses have Baiyun wrong and the surnames swapped.

sense_errors: 'The commentaries apply this to Wang Yan and Cao Shuang' misreads 訓注 as commentaries
names_garbled: Baiyun is glossed as Gao Hedai; it is Guo Yong
Y.comment: Misreads 訓注 as 'commentaries' and misidentifies Baiyun.

omissions: 訓注 (Li Xun and Zheng Zhu) is left out of the list of examples
names_garbled: Baiyun is glossed as Gao Hedai; it is Guo Yong
Z.comment: Drops Li Xun and Zheng Zhu from the examples and misidentifies Baiyun.

W.comment: Accurate. The margin characters, which are a garbled running head, are translated literally inside unclear tags, which does no harm. 'Sinking into danger' slightly over-expands 陷.

X.comment: Faithful and complete. It correctly flags the margin characters and stops on the phrase that runs over to the next page.

Y.comment: Faithful. The trigram identifications are kept in notes, and the extra glosses ('speaking', 'brilliance') are minor elaborations.

Z.comment: Faithful and somewhat wordy. It ends on 'which cannot' at the page break, exactly where the source breaks off.

omissions: opening fragment 亂者也 ('…cannot be disordered') not rendered
W.comment: Accurate and complete apart from the three-character fragment that ends the previous page's sentence. 'Wind then blows' slightly weakens the sense of dependence in 因有所吹噓.

X.comment: Faithful and complete; the notes are harmless.

Y.comment: Faithful and complete. Rendering 相摩 as 'interact and stimulate' is acceptable.

Z.comment: Faithful and complete.

W.comment: Faithful throughout. Reading 牧 as 'official herdsmen' and 出葆 as 'leads out the garrison' are defensible choices.

sense_errors: 'the defender alone holds ultimate authority' for 守獨智 (it means only the defender knows the prognostications)
X.comment: Close rendering with one minor slip on 守獨智. 'Brings forth stored provisions' for 出葆 is a debatable reading.

omissions: 若工 (artisans) not rendered
sense_errors: 'High officials, herdsmen of the people' splits 望氣舍近守官 wrongly, taking 官 into the next clause
Y.comment: Mostly sound. It misparses 守官/牧 and drops the minor item 'artisans', but the gist survives.

Z.comment: Faithful. Rendering 官牧 as 'district magistrates' and making 縣師 plural are minor interpretive choices.

sense_errors: 'Before marching out against the enemy, the duke... shall take solemn defensive oaths... and only then retire': 先於戎乃退 belongs to the invocators' rites, not to the duke's oath, and the order is changed
W.comment: Faithful and complete apart from a muddled final sentence that moves 先於戎乃退 onto the duke.

sense_errors: 'counterfeit calls' / 'deceptive signals' for 譟 (shouting in unison), though it is close enough
X.comment: Complete; reads the obscure 移中中處澤 loosely and treats the shouting as deception, but the overall sense holds.

Y.comment: Accurate and complete; ends on the oath, with its content on the next page.

sense_errors: 'Gather dogs, swine, piglets, and chickens to feed on the grain': the source means eat their flesh (食其實), not let the animals eat grain
'urgent matters from the marshes' takes 澤 too literally
Z.comment: Complete, but gets the livestock clause backwards: the animals are fed instead of being eaten.

W.comment: Faithful. Some phrasing is rough ("drums were beaten in contest", "In detail, this king has declared"), but the meaning is kept.

sense_errors: "We are the rightful ones!" is an invented reading of 唯乃是王
X.comment: Mostly accurate. "white flag for stone" only finishes the clause split at the page edge, so it is not bleed. The opening has one minor misreading.

sense_errors: "I shall certainly cherish the resolve to avenge this, lest they destroy your altars": the threat to destroy the altars is the enemy king's, but it is given to the duke
"Their detailed design is solely to claim kingship over us" misreads 詳唯乃是王
"At the corners, skilled archers were positioned": 于隅 belongs with the 旌 banner
names_garbled: 旂 rendered "falcon banner" (it is a dragon banner)
Y.comment: The oath speech is rewritten so the duke appears to make the enemy's threat.

sense_errors: "Truly, such is your king!" wrongly makes the defenders' own king the unprincipled one
names_garbled: 旂 rendered "falcon banner" (it is a dragon banner)
Z.comment: The rest is acceptable, but the opening of the oath points the blame at the wrong king.

sense_errors: 'stockpiles of stores for wells and hearths' misreads 井竈有處 (wells and stoves must have designated places)
W.comment: Complete and generally accurate; one misparse in the wells/hearths item, otherwise faithful with acceptable glosses.

X.comment: Complete and accurate; 'massed reserve troops' for 多卒 is a slight overreach but harmless.

omissions: opening '為白旗' (white flag, for stones per the previous page) not rendered
sense_errors: 'and then lowers the flag' wrongly makes the supply officer the one who lowers it
names_garbled: 莊旗 rendered as 'halberd flag'
Y.comment: Drops the white-flag clause at the top of the page; the rest is concise and mostly accurate.

additions: 'for each rank' added to the tallies clause
'for each post' added to the laws clause
sense_errors: 重質有居 rendered as 'secure quarters for heavy valuables' instead of hostages
names_garbled: 倉英之旗 as 'dark-spotted eagle flag'
梯末之旗 as 'ladder-and-mattock flag'
Z.comment: Complete but has small inventions and mistranslates the hostages as valuables; the flag names are loosely rendered.

V.comment: Complete, accurate rendering of the whole page.

omissions: 故云婦 — that the text says 'woman' because the other lines are yin — is lost
sense_errors: 'because the other lines are all yin, it is said that the second line can embrace and accept' wrongly ties 故云 to 二能包納 instead of explaining 'woman'
W.comment: The rest is accurate, but the clause explaining why the line text says 'woman' is garbled into a different statement.

X.comment: Accurate and complete; the explanatory note is acceptable.

Y.comment: Accurate and complete.

omissions: 以尊卑言之五父道也二子道也 (the fifth line as the father's way, the second as the son's way) is missing
sense_errors: 'if she still accepts what is good, her clarity will become wide' makes the woman the subject; the source means the second line should accept the woman's good and so widen its own clarity
Z.comment: Leaves out the father/son status sentence and reverses who accepts what is good in the first passage.

W.comment: Complete and accurate. It reads the line statement as one sentence, following Cheng Yi's reading, which is acceptable. Leaving out the running title is not a fault.

X.comment: Complete and faithful. Rendering 不順 as 'contrary to what is right' is a loose word choice, not a sense error. The notes are fine.

Y.comment: Complete and accurate. 'her own virtue and person' slightly expands 保有其身, but this is minor.

Z.comment: Complete and accurate, with slightly expansive wording such as 'enveloped darkness and youthful folly'.

W.comment: Complete and accurate; it correctly identifies Baiyun as Guo Yong and Yichuan as Cheng Yi.

names_garbled: Baiyun glossed as 'Gao Hesun' (should be Guo Yong 郭雍)
X.comment: The body text is complete and accurate, but the note misidentifies Baiyun.

Y.comment: Complete and accurate; the closing quotation mark is placed slightly too late, after 是其所以困也, which is minor.

names_garbled: Baiyun glossed as 'Guo Xiangzheng' (should be Guo Yong 郭雍)
Z.comment: The body text is complete and accurate, but the gloss misidentifies Baiyun.

sense_errors: Analects quote rendered as 'these the common people consider to be the lowest sort'; the line actually means such people are the lowest among the people
W.comment: Complete and mostly accurate; the Analects quote is slightly misconstrued.

sense_errors: 'which makes the common people the lowest class' misreads 民斯為下 (such people are the lowest)
X.comment: Complete and faithful apart from awkward handling of the Analects quote.

sense_errors: 吝 rendered 'called distress' and 困吝 as 'distress and entanglement', which muddles the 困/吝 distinction
Y.comment: Complete; the term 吝 is rendered loosely, but the overall sense holds.

Z.comment: Complete and accurate; the omitted footer is only a running head.

additions: "Specially Promoted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness" — this title is not in the source
names_garbled: 司徒 rendered "Minister of Works" (should be Minister of Education)
W.comment: Adds a title the source lacks (特進光祿大夫-type) to the father's titles and mistranslates 司徒; the rest is accurate.

X.comment: Complete and accurate; "Specially Appointed Officer" for 開府儀同三司 is loose but acceptable.

names_garbled: 司徒 rendered "Minister of Works"
開府儀同三司 rendered "Palace Emissary with the Threefold Dignities"
Y.comment: Complete and faithful in sense; two official titles are mis-rendered, though the notes give the original terms.

sense_errors: 并為公 rendered "honor both sides as dukes" (it means all three generations were made dukes)
Z.comment: Complete; one awkward misreading of 并為公 and "Pillar of the State" drops "Upper", but otherwise accurate.

names_garbled: 'Prince Yiwang' for 懿文太子 (should be Crown Prince Yiwen)
gloss gives Dezu as 'Zhu Baoliu' (should be Zhu Bailiu)
W.comment: Accurate overall; 于厥後 is read as opening a new sentence rather than completing 'in their posterity'; the crown prince's name is garbled.

X.comment: Faithful and complete; correctly reads 于厥後 as finishing the previous page's sentence.

names_garbled: gloss makes Dezu the great-grandfather 'Zhu Chuyi' (Zhu Chuyi is Yizu; Dezu is the great-great-grandfather Zhu Bailiu)
Y.comment: Accurate text; the Dezu gloss is factually wrong, and 'transmit confidence' for 傳信 is weak wording.

sense_errors: 'Later, descendants included ... Zhu Fu' turns 朱浮裔 (the Ming line descends from Zhu Fu) into Zhu Fu being one of the descendants
Z.comment: Generally faithful; the Zhu Fu descent clause is slightly misparsed.

W.comment: Complete and accurate. '潭王梓趙王杞' is handled as Prince of Tan and Prince of Zhao, Zhu Qi, and 靳獻王 is correctly read as Qi.

additions: 'Fisherman's Cave, Fourth Month, Complete' renders the garbled running head 欽定四庫全書 as if it were real text (it is tagged unclear)
names_garbled: 'King Tan of Zai, King Zhao of Qi' misreads 潭王梓趙王杞: 梓 and 杞 are the princes' personal names, not fiefs
X.comment: Complete, but the Tan/Zhao entries are garbled into wrong titles. 'Jin' for 靳 is a literal reading.

names_garbled: note 'Zhu Zhi' for King Xian of Han (should be Zhu Song)
note 'Zhu Huo' for Commoner of Gu (should be Zhu Hui)
notes for King Xian of Jing / King Huai of Teng give the wrong personal names (Jing is Zhu Zhangang)
Y.comment: The body text is complete and accurate. Several of the many identification notes give wrong personal names.

names_garbled: 'Prince Zhao of Zi' garbles 潭王梓趙王杞: 梓 is the Prince of Tan's personal name, not part of the Zhao title
Z.comment: Complete. 'Civil Emperor' for 文皇帝 is very literal, and the Zhao entry is mangled.

W.comment: Complete and accurate. All names and counts match the source.

X.comment: Complete and accurate. Calling the princes 'King' is a style choice, and the Ruizong note is correct.

names_garbled: note on King Jian of Ji gives 'Zhu Jianchun' (same as Xu Dao; actually Zhu Jianjun 見浚)
note on Third Imperial Prince gives 'Zhu Jianpei' (same as Hui Zhuang)
note on King Huai of Xiu gives 'Zhu Jianjin' (should be Zhu Jianshu 見澍)
Y.comment: The translation body is complete and accurate. Several personal names in the notes are wrong or repeated.

sense_errors: 'Emperor Xianzong had fourteen sons': the source says 十三子 (thirteen)
names_garbled: 'Crown Prince Huaiqian' for 懷獻 (Huaixian)
note on Prince Zhuang of De gives 'Zhu Jianwan' (should be Zhu Jianlin 見潾)
note on Prince Huai of Xiu gives 'Zhu Jianpei'
Z.comment: The body gives the wrong number of Xianzong's sons and garbles the name Huaixian. Several names in the notes are also wrong.

sense_errors: 'I have granted everything they asked. Regarding the matters of the High Ministers' misparses 吾皆許之上大夫之事 (he promised them senior-minister office)
'If one serves the lord of the altars' for 苟主社稷 (if someone is master of the altars)
W.comment: Mostly faithful. It misparses the promise of senior-minister office, and the misread folio mark 罵 is translated (marked unclear).

X.comment: Accurate throughout and correctly reads 許之上大夫之事 as a promise of high office.

sense_errors: 'I have granted everything they asked. Concerning the affairs of senior ministers' misparses 吾皆許之上大夫之事
Y.comment: Faithful apart from the common misparse of the senior-minister promise. The misread folio mark is rendered as 'curses'.

sense_errors: 'I will reward them all. Concerning the matters of the senior ministers' misparses 吾皆許之上大夫之事
Z.comment: Faithful apart from the misparse of the senior-minister promise. The misread folio mark is rendered as 'scolding'.

W.comment: Complete and accurate; calling 詩傳 the 'Mao Commentary' is a debatable label, not a real error.

X.comment: Complete and accurate; the 678 BCE date note is correct.

Y.comment: Body text is accurate. Two notes are wrong: the year should be 678 BCE, not 696 BCE, and the guess that 詩傳 means Hanshi Waizhuan is doubtful. 'Full measure of years' is a slight stretch for 就盈數.

Z.comment: Complete and accurate.

names_garbled: note glosses Wei (子亹) as 'Zizhong'
W.comment: Complete and accurate. Only the explanatory note for 子亹 is wrong.

names_garbled: note glosses Wei (子亹) as 'Duke Zimin'
X.comment: Complete and faithful. One note gives a doubtful name for 子亹.

names_garbled: note glosses Wei (子亹) as 'Zizhong'
Y.comment: Complete and accurate. 'Regained' for 得國 is loose, and the note for 子亹 is wrong.

Z.comment: Complete and accurate, with no notes but no errors.

names_garbled: 'Huai' for 袤/袲 (meeting place, read Mao in the OCR)
W.comment: Complete and accurate; the meeting-place name is wrong and there is a small slip, 'constant constancy'.

X.comment: Accurate and complete, with helpful notes; 'Ji Zhong' is a common variant reading of 祭仲.

Y.comment: Accurate; it finishes the broken phrase at the page edge ('without punishment', slightly loose for 無恙), and 'covenanted' for 會 is a minor overstatement.

Z.comment: Faithful and complete rendering of the page.

names_garbled: 滑稽傳 rendered as 'Biographies of Huaiyin and Sunshu Ao'
W.comment: Correctly identifies the carry-over 丨丨 as Ba Qiu (巴丘); accurate overall apart from a garbled chapter title.

additions: 'the divine spirits of Ling Hill' (divine spirits not in source)
sense_errors: Yuan Jie and Li Kuo lines given as 'Ling Hill' instead of Ba Qiu (巴丘) from the previous entry
names_garbled: 巴丘 rendered as Ling Hill
滑稽傳 rendered as 'Biography of Weiji'
X.comment: Puts the wrong hill in the two carry-over poems that belong to the 巴丘 entry; also garbles a chapter title.

omissions: Liu Shao rhapsody: 靈丘 dropped from 'level garden' clause
sense_errors: Yuan Jie and Li Kuo lines given as 'Ling Qiu' instead of Ba Qiu (巴丘)
names_garbled: 巴丘 rendered as Ling Qiu
滑稽傳 rendered as 'Biographies of the Scribes'
Y.comment: Puts the wrong hill in the carry-over poems, drops Ling Qiu from Liu Shao's line, and garbles the 滑稽傳 title.

sense_errors: 白鳳之肺 rendered as 'liver' instead of lung
carry-over poems given as 'Wine Gourd Hill (Hu Qiu)' instead of Ba Qiu
names_garbled: 巴丘 rendered as Hu Qiu / Wine Gourd Hill
高氏山 rendered as 'Gao Mountain'
趙世家 called 'Basic Annals'
Z.comment: Misidentifies the carry-over hill as Hu Qiu, gives 'liver' for 肺 (lung), and has several smaller name slips.

sense_errors: Sima Xiangru passage: 'yet it was so slight that it was extinguished by burning brushwood' misreads 隕杭休之以燎 (the fish fell into the boat and the omen was honoured with a burnt offering)
names_garbled: 'Longqiu Zhang' for 萇 (should be Chang)
'Tamo' for 太末 (Taimo)
W.comment: Mostly accurate and complete, but the opening Sima Xiangru clause is garbled into a wrong meaning.

additions: 'when he reached the sacrificial platform a fire flared up' is commentary-style padding not in the source
sense_errors: 'yet King Wu regarded these as trivial': the source calls the omens trivial; King Wu is not the one judging them
ballad 'The two Shen and Liu families' drops the two 傳/傅 (Fu Yan and his son)
names_garbled: 'Shen Yan and his son Shen Xian': Yan is of the 傳/傅 family, not Shen
'Longqiu Zhang' for 萇 (Chang)
X.comment: Sima Xiangru passage is padded and misattributed, and the Qiu Zhongfu ballad gets the magistrates' families wrong.

additions: 'and the shooting star' is invented from 隕
sense_errors: 'Grand Protection's rise and fall': 太保 is the title Grand Protector, so the subject is mangled
names_garbled: 'Inscription on the Stone Crane' for 瘞鶴銘
'Tamo' for 太末 (Taimo)
'jackals' for 貉 (badgers)
Y.comment: Adds a non-existent 'shooting star' omen and garbles the Xie An title; otherwise complete.

names_garbled: 'Grand Protection' for 太保 (Grand Protector)
'Longqiu Zhang' for 萇 (Chang)
Z.comment: Complete and faithful; only minor naming slips.

names_garbled: 'Lv Anshi said' treats 呂安世說 as a person; it should read 百姓以安 followed by the book title Shishuo
W.comment: Complete and accurate. The only slip is reading 世說 as a person 'Lv Anshi', and the OCR caused that.

names_garbled: 'Xun of Lingling' should be Langling (荀朗陵)
'Zhang of Longqiu' should be Longqiu Chang (萇)
X.comment: Complete and faithful. It has minor name slips (Lingling, Zhang), and its meta tag repeats the previous page's line, but only inside the tag.

names_garbled: 'The Magistrate of Longqiu' should be Longqiu Chang (萇), a person's name
'Lü An's Worldly Talk' garbles 以安 + Shishuo
Y.comment: Complete. It reads 丨丨萇 as an official title and makes 呂安 the author of Shishuo, both prompted by the OCR.

names_garbled: 'The Magistrate of Longqiu' should be Longqiu Chang (萇)
Z.comment: Complete and accurate apart from reading 萇 as a magistrate's title. 'southern barbarians' and 'tether the Great Gale' are loose wording only.

W.comment: Complete and accurate. The Qingqiu continuation, San Qiu, Xuan Qiu, Shou Qiu and Zao Qiu are all rendered faithfully.

names_garbled: 契 rendered 'Qi' instead of Xie
X.comment: Complete and generally accurate. The only flaw is the misreading of 契 as 'Qi'; 'swallow' for 烏 follows the traditional story.

omissions: 匈剖 (her chest split open) left out: it says only 'conceived, and gave birth to Xie'
Y.comment: Otherwise accurate, but it drops the clause about Xie being born when Jiandi's chest split open.

names_garbled: headword 青丘 rendered 'Sangqiu (Mulberry Mound)' throughout
子虛賦 titled 'Rhapsody on the Imperial Hunt'
句芒 rendered 'Jumang' instead of Goumang
Z.comment: Misreads the continuing headword 青丘 as Sangqiu throughout the first entry and garbles other names.
